outcome: No accepted resolution of Beal's conjecture is found as of 11 Oct 2026. Since 26 Jan 2024 the events are unrefereed full-proof claims (Vega 2024; Harris, Hanners and Aabidi El Moussati 2025; Preprints.org manuscripts 2025-26; Davlatov's arXiv entry, Beal content dated Jan-Mar 2026 and partly withdrawn), an IUT-based reduction that leaves 2446 signatures open (Zhou, arXiv 2510.05448, Oct 2025), two papers that explicitly do not resolve it (Feinstein, Sept 2025; Huckstead, June 2026), a Devpost project on the open signature (3,5,7) (July 2026, not opened), and an unconditional claim for the single signature (5,5,23) in a GitHub repository created 9 Oct 2026, whose commits name Claude Opus 5.5 as co-author and whose novelty is stated by its author as not yet confirmed.
problem_asks: Beal's conjecture (Wikipedia, January 2024 wording): for all positive integers A, B, C, x, y, z with x, y, z > 2 and A^x + B^y = C^z, the three numbers A, B, C have a common prime factor. Parts: (1) it quantifies over every exponent triple (x, y, z) with all three exponents at least 3, i.e. infinitely many signatures up to permutation; (2) for each triple, over all solutions in positive integers; (3) the conclusion is that one prime divides all of A, B and C. Equivalent forms, all standard: no solution with gcd(A, B, C) = 1, and no solution with A, B, C pairwise coprime. These are equivalent, because a prime dividing two of A, B, C divides A^x + B^y = C^z and therefore divides the third. So a result on one signature asks only for that signature's part, and a claim to settle the pairwise-coprime case is a claim to settle the whole conjecture. The article also records the names Mauldin conjecture and Tijdeman-Zagier conjecture, and notes that the case x = y = z is Fermat's Last Theorem.

events.what_happened: Darmon and Granville (1995): for each fixed exponent triple with 1/p + 1/q + 1/r < 1, only finitely many coprime solutions of the generalised Fermat equation exist (ineffective). Darmon and Merel (1995): no solutions for signature (n, n, 2), n >= 4. Both are recorded from the Wikipedia article's list of partial results, which I opened; the original papers were not opened.
events.delivers: Finiteness of coprime solutions for each individual exponent triple (ineffective, no list of solutions); nonexistence for signatures (n, n, 2), n >= 4. Restricted to fixed triples and to the listed signature.
events.remains: The universal statement over all exponent triples; for each triple, whether solutions exist and whether they all have a common prime factor.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: finiteness and nonexistence, not counterexamples.

events.what_happened: Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem (x = y = z = n >= 3 has no positive solutions), listed on the Wikipedia article as the diagonal case of Beal's conjecture. The Wikipedia list gives 1994; the widely cited publication year is 1995. Recorded from the Wikipedia article; the original paper was not opened.
events.revisions: Wikipedia gives 1994, search results give 1995; the year is not settled by the sources I read.
events.delivers: The diagonal slice x = y = z of Beal's conjecture: no solutions in positive integers with all three exponents equal to n >= 3, so no coprime solutions on the diagonal.
events.remains: Every exponent triple that is not all-equal.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on the diagonal.

events.what_happened: Poonen (1998): signature (3, 5, 5) settled, as listed on the Wikipedia article (citation [26]). Recorded from that list; the paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Nonexistence of coprime solutions for signature (3, 5, 5) only.
events.remains: Every other signature.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on this signature.

events.what_happened: Mihailescu's proof of Catalan's conjecture (2002), which the Wikipedia article uses to exclude the case A = 1 or B = 1 of Beal's equation. Recorded from the article; the paper was not opened.
events.delivers: The sub-case in which one of the bases equals 1 has no solutions with exponents above 2.
events.remains: Every case in which all bases exceed 1.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Group of signature-specific results cited on the Wikipedia article's list: Bruin (2003) for (2, 3, 8), (2, 3, 9) and (2, 4, 5); Poonen, Schaefer and Stoll (2005) for (2, 3, 7); Bennett, Ellenberg and Ng (2009) for (2, 4, n), n >= 6; Zureick-Brown (2009) for (2, 3, 10); Freitas, Naskrecki and Stoll for (2, 3, 11). Recorded from the Wikipedia list; the papers were not opened individually.
events.revisions: Dates run from 2003 to 2009 across the group; the group is dated by its earliest member.
events.delivers: Nonexistence of coprime solutions for each listed signature only.
events.remains: All other signatures, including all those with no listed result.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on these signatures.

events.what_happened: Group of results cited on the Wikipedia article's list: Bennett (2006) for (2n, 2n, 5), n >= 2; Bennett and Chen (2011) and Bennett, Chen, Dahmen and Yazdani (2014) for (2, 6, n) and related families, including (2, 2n, 3) for 3 <= n <= 107 except n = 7 and modular congruences for prime n, (2, 2n, 9), (2, 2n, 10), (2, 2n, 15), (3, 6, n), (2n, 3, 4) and (3, 3, n) for 3 <= n <= 109; Siksek and Stoll (2011) for (3, 4, 5); Siksek and Stoll (2013) for (2, 3, 15); Dahmen and Siksek (2013) for (5, 5, 7), (5, 5, 19) and (7, 7, 5); Anni and Siksek for (2l, 2m, n), n = 3, 5, 7, 11; Billerey et al. for (2l, 2m, 13); Kraus for (3l, 3m, n). Recorded from the Wikipedia list; the papers were not opened individually and some entries are undated on the list.
events.revisions: Dates run from 2006 to 2014 on the list; some group members are undated there. Dated by the earliest member.
events.delivers: Nonexistence of coprime solutions for each listed signature or family. Restricted to those signatures; the Bennett et al. families cover only the stated exponent patterns, and the list does not give their full exponent ranges.
events.remains: Every signature not listed, and the listed families outside their stated ranges.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on these signatures.

events.what_happened: Dahmen and Siksek (2013): generalised Fermat equations with signatures (5, 5, 7), (5, 5, 19) and (7, 7, 5) have no non-trivial primitive solutions (unconditional, per the Wikipedia list). From a search snippet of the survey, they also treat (5, 5, 11), (5, 5, 13) and (7, 7, 11) assuming GRH. The survey (Ratcliffe and Grechuk, Table 1.1) lists (5, 5, 7) and (5, 5, 19) as solved and does not list (5, 5, 23). The snippet for the GRH cases was not opened.
events.delivers: Unconditional nonexistence for signatures (5, 5, 7), (5, 5, 19) and (7, 7, 5); GRH-conditional for (5, 5, 11), (5, 5, 13), (7, 7, 11) (snippet only).
events.remains: (5, 5, 23) and all other signatures.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on these signatures.

events.what_happened: Michael Stoll, 'Chabauty without the Mordell-Weil group' (arXiv:1506.04286, first posted 13 June 2015, v2 3 Jan 2017). The abstract names generalised Fermat equations x^5 + y^5 = z^p as an application. Its introduction states that the curves 5y^2 = 4x^p + 1 have only the three obvious rational points 'when p is a prime <= 53 (assuming GRH for p >= 23)', and that by Dahmen and Siksek this gives that the only coprime integer solutions of x^5 + y^5 = z^p are trivial. Read from the abstract and the ar5iv introduction; Section 8 and Theorem 8.8 were not reached in the fetch.
events.revisions: v1 13 Jun 2015; v2 3 Jan 2017 (abstract listing).
events.delivers: Signature (5, 5, p) for each prime p <= 53, with the p >= 23 cases conditional on GRH per the introduction. The conditional status of p = 23 is the prior state of signature (5, 5, 23).
events.remains: The GRH-free status for p >= 23; all signatures other than (5, 5, p).
events.doubts: The GRH dependence is as stated in the introduction; Theorem 8.8, the exact result, was not read. The 2026 beals repository says its Theorem 8.8 is the prior GRH-conditional result for p = 23.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on (5, 5, p) for the listed primes, conditional on GRH for p >= 23.

events.what_happened: Peter Norvig, 'Beal's Conjecture Revisited' (page dated 22 Oct 2015, revised 28 Oct 2015 and 4 July 2017): a computer search for counterexamples. The page also reports a distributed C++ search by Witold Jarnicki and David Konerding covering bases up to 200,000 and exponents up to 5,000. No counterexample found. The Wikipedia article summarises the ranges as x, y, z <= 7 with A, B, C <= 250,000 and as x, y, z <= 100 with A, B, C <= 10,000; the page read gives other parameters.
events.revisions: Revised 28 Oct 2015 and 4 Jul 2017.
events.delivers: No counterexample within the searched bounds. A finite search of instances of a universal claim; it moves no quantity the conjecture names.
events.remains: The whole conjecture; every triple beyond the searched range.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture within the searched range.

events.what_happened: Nicholas J. Daras, 'A Constructive Proof of Beal's Conjecture' (arXiv:1903.03613, math.GM, 4 pages, one version, 8 Mar 2019). The entire abstract reads: 'We prove that there is no non-trivial integral positive solution to the generalized Fermat equation.' The body was not opened, and the abstract does not restrict to pairwise coprime bases.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: As abstracted, a claim to the full conjecture (no non-trivial positive solution to the generalised Fermat equation). The abstract does not define 'non-trivial' or specify the exponent conditions.
events.remains: None, if the abstract's claim held. No argument was read.
events.doubts: Unreviewed (math.GM); single 4-page version; the body was not read, and the abstract's scope is not stated in the Beal form. No engagement found in searches.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture (no solutions), as claimed.

events.what_happened: 'Discovery on Beal Conjecture', AfricArXiv repository record 1/1189 (Preprint collection). The page states 'In this paper we give a proof for Beal's conjecture' and gives no author or date. The author (Idriss Olivier Bado) and the year 2019 come from a search snippet, not from the page.
events.delivers: As stated, a claim to the full conjecture. No argument visible on the record page.
events.remains: None, if the claim held.
events.doubts: The record page gives no body, author or date; the year and author come from a search snippet. No engagement found.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, as claimed.

events.what_happened: 'Definitive Proof of Beal's Conjecture', EasyChair preprint by Abdelmajid Ben Hadj Salem, 2019. Known only from a search result title and snippet; the EasyChair page was not opened.
events.delivers: As titled, a claim to the full conjecture. Content not read.
events.remains: None, if the claim held.
events.doubts: Not opened; claim known from the title only. Not peer reviewed on the EasyChair platform.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, as titled.

events.what_happened: Zhong-Peng Zhou, 'The inter-universal Teichmuller theory and new Diophantine results over the rational numbers. I' (arXiv:2503.14510, math.NT, one version, 8 Mar 2025). Abstract: explicit bounds on log(x^r y^s z^t) for primitive solutions of x^r + y^s = z^t via inter-universal Teichmuller theory (IUT); an effective abc constant of 400; an unconditional alternative proof of FLT for prime exponents >= 11; and a computation reported to show no non-trivial primitive solutions when r, s, t >= 20, or when (r, s, t) is a permutation of (3, 3, n), n >= 3. The paper does not mention Beal's conjecture in its abstract or text read.
events.revisions: v1 only (arXiv listing read).
events.delivers: For the generalised Fermat equation x^r + y^s = z^t: a claimed exclusion of primitive solutions for all exponents >= 20 (computational) and for (3, 3, n). Read as a Beal-type claim, it would cover Beal signatures with every exponent >= 20 if the computation is correct. The paper does not state that consequence for Beal.
events.remains: Beal signatures with some exponent below 20, other than (3, 3, n), n >= 3, as the abstract states.
events.doubts: Rests on IUT. Scholze and Stix (2018) said that a key step, Corollary 3.12 of IUT III, had a gap they called 'serious, unfixable' (Scientific American, 2020, opened); Mochizuki disputes this. Press coverage exists; I found no mathematical engagement with Zhou's paper. The computation is described only in the abstract as read.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture (no solutions) for the exponent ranges claimed; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Frank Vega, 'Note for the Beal's Conjecture' (EasyChair Preprint 13256; Cambridge Open Engage copy, working paper). Versions: v1 11 May 2024, v2 29 May 2024, v3 3 June 2024 (the version read). The v3 abstract says the paper 'presents a short proof of the Beal's Conjecture' and also says 'Beal's Conjecture remains unproven, and a significant prize is offered for a solution'. The proof is not on the page read.
events.revisions: v1 11 May 2024; v2 29 May 2024; v3 3 Jun 2024 (Working Paper).
events.delivers: As abstracted, a claim to the full conjecture; no argument visible.
events.remains: None, if the claim held.
events.doubts: The abstract is internally inconsistent ('short proof' and 'remains unproven'). The page itself says it is an 'early or alternative research output' not peer reviewed by Cambridge University Press. No proof text read; no engagement found.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, as claimed.

events.what_happened: Frank Vega, 'A Note on the Beal Conjecture' (EasyChair Preprint 13819, dated 3 July 2024 on the page read; search snippets show further dates of 5 and 6 July 2024, presumably other versions). Abstract: 'Combining short and basic tools, we were able to prove the Beal conjecture', and 'The present work potentially offers a solution which is closer in spirit to Fermat's original idea.' No proof text on the page read.
events.revisions: Version dates 3, 5 and 6 July 2024 seen in search snippets; the v1 page read is dated 3 July 2024.
events.delivers: As abstracted, a claim to the full conjecture; no argument visible.
events.remains: None, if the claim held.
events.doubts: The same author's May 2024 note says the conjecture remains unproven. EasyChair preprint, not peer reviewed. No engagement found.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, as claimed.

events.what_happened: 'Elementary Proof of Beal's Conjecture [v2]', Preprints.org manuscript 202501.1436 (title and ID from a search result). The page returned HTTP 403 and was not opened. Date inferred from the manuscript ID prefix (202501); author not seen.
events.revisions: A v2 is indicated by the title; v1 not seen.
events.delivers: As titled, a claim to the full conjecture. Not read.
events.remains: None, if the claim held.
events.doubts: Not opened; date and author are not confirmed. Preprints.org marks such items as not peer reviewed.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, as titled.

events.what_happened: Michael Hanners (Legacy Alliance Research Division), 'Resolution of Beal's Conjecture' (Zenodo record 19401153, listed as version 7, 'Published May 2, 2025'). The abstract says it resolves the conjecture 'via entropy minimization and Hanners Theorem' using a 'Harmonic Coherence (HC) framework', with assumptions A1 (CER identity), A2 (HC transport) and A3 (spectral gap), and reports a '65-test replication battery' finding 'no zero crossings and no coprime counterexamples up to N = 500'. The page states 'We resolve Beal's Conjecture'.
events.revisions: Version 7 listed, published 2 May 2025; the earliest version is not visible. The record also shows 'Created and modified: April 3, 2026', which conflicts with the May 2025 publication date.
events.delivers: As stated, a claim to the full conjecture. The numerical battery covers N <= 500 and is evidence only.
events.remains: None, if the claim held.
events.time_since_posted: about 17 months from the v7 date
events.doubts: Self-published on Zenodo with a single listed affiliation; the 'Harmonic Coherence' framework and 'Hanners Theorem' are not found in any other source searched; the numerical battery is bounded at N = 500; the record's dates conflict. No engagement found.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, as claimed.

events.what_happened: Abdeslam Aabidi El Moussati, 'A Formal Resolution of the Beal Conjecture via Symbolic Ancestry and Arithmetic Embedding' (Cambridge Open Engage working paper, DOI 10.33774/coe-2025-84f5x, posted 25 May 2025). Abstract: 'We present a formal resolution of the Beal Conjecture by embedding symbolic ancestry from the AION framework into classical number theory'; it argues that a shared 'symbolic ancestor' guarantees a common divisor, 'thereby confirming the Beal Conjecture structurally'. The page states it 'has not been peer-reviewed by Cambridge University Press at the time of posting'.
events.revisions: Version 1 only seen.
events.delivers: As stated, a claim to the full conjecture.
events.remains: None, if the claim held.
events.doubts: The argument's key step (a shared symbolic ancestor forces a shared prime divisor) is asserted in the abstract, not derived there. The 'formal' in the title is not a proof assistant: no Lean or Coq artifact is named. 'AION framework' is not described on the page, which does not call it an AI tool.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, as claimed.

events.what_happened: Lemuel Schaine Harris, 'Proof of Beal's Conjecture Cuboid-Valuation Method' (Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15983835, CC BY 4.0; record 'Issued' 13 Jul 2025, published 16 Jul 2025 on the record page, version 7 shown). The abstract claims 'an elementary, contradiction-based proof' for pairwise coprime A, B, C > 1 and exponents > 2, using a cuboid construction and four cases (a Fermat-type contradiction ruling out gcd(x, y, z) > 1, a gap argument, Zsigmondy/LTE arguments, and a pairwise-coprimality argument), and says 'Combining these methods completes an unconditional proof of Beal's Conjecture.' The record gives the author's affiliation as the University of Florida.
events.revisions: Version 7 shown; a newer version is noted on the page. Earlier versions not seen.
events.delivers: As stated, a claim to the full conjecture (the pairwise-coprime form is equivalent to the full statement).
events.remains: None, if the claim held.
events.doubts: Self-published Zenodo preprint with no peer review stated. The full proof text was not read, so the four cases are the author's own summary. No engagement found.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, as claimed.

events.what_happened: Preda Mihailescu, 'On a Popular Diophantine Norm Equation' (arXiv:2108.08572, v1 19 Aug 2021; comments 'Submitted, under review'). Abstract: 'We show that the equation (x^p + y^p)/(x + y) = p^e z^p has no solutions in coprime integers x, y, z, with a prime exponent p > 89 and e in {0, 1}', via a new 'adelic approximation' method. This is a factored form of the Fermat-Catalan equation, not x^p + y^p = z^r.
events.revisions: v1 19 Aug 2021; v2 14 Oct 2021; v3 10 Oct 2022 (retitled 'Semilocal approximation for the Fermat-Catalan and further popular Diophantine norm equations'); v4 22 Sep 2025 (retitled 'Beyond and slightly aside of the Fermat desert', authors Boris Bartolome and Preda Mihailescu). See the separate v3 and v4 events.
events.delivers: A nonexistence claim for the factored equation (x^p + y^p)/(x + y) = p^e z^p with prime p > 89. It does not state a result for x^p + y^p = z^r, and the Beal equation is not its subject. As a claim about a different equation, it settles no Beal signature on its own statement.
events.remains: The Beal statement for every signature; the factored equation for p <= 89.
events.doubts: Under review per its own comments field, not published as of the versions read. Scope differs across versions (see v3 and v4 events).
events.direction: Toward nonexistence for the factored equation; not directly toward the Beal equation.

events.what_happened: Mihailescu, 'Semilocal approximation for the Fermat-Catalan and further popular Diophantine norm equations' (arXiv:2108.08572, v3 revised 10 Oct 2022). Abstract: '(x^p + y^p)/(x + y) = p^e z^q has no solutions in coprime integers x, y, z', for prime exponents q >= p >= 5 and e in {0, 1}, with an absolute bound for q < p; it states that this 'provides, in particular, a complete cyclotomic proof of Fermat's Last Theorem'. The page does not claim a result for x^p + y^p = z^r. Earlier versions were not read; this is the first version seen with the q >= p >= 5 claim.
events.delivers: Nonexistence for the factored equation with q >= p >= 5. Not stated for the unfactored Beal equation. The survey (Ratcliffe and Grechuk, footnote 5) and Zhou's background list may be describing this line of work, though their wording (r > 3 sqrt(p log2 p) on the (p, p, r) signature) does not appear in the versions I read.
events.remains: Beal for every signature; the factored equation for q < p.
events.doubts: Under review per the comments field. The claimed result is for a different equation from Beal's, and the arXiv abstract's scope does not include the (5, 5, q) condition that Zhou's paper attributes to this citation. Version 2 (14 Oct 2021) was not read.
events.direction: Toward nonexistence for the factored equation; not directly toward the Beal equation.

events.what_happened: Boris Bartolome and Preda Mihailescu, 'Beyond and slightly aside of the Fermat desert' (arXiv:2108.08572, v4 22 Sep 2025; comments 'Submitted, under review'). Abstract (as read in the HTML version): the factored equation (x^p + y^p)/(x + y) = p^e z^p has no solutions in coprime non-zero integers x, y, z for a prime p > 3, with e in {0, 1}, and the authors say this gives a new cyclotomic proof of FLT. The HTML header is dated 'Version 1.0 August 24, 2026', which conflicts with the arXiv stamp of 22 Sep 2025. 'Recent history' is a placeholder reading '(To be reinserted after complete referee's review of the paper)'. The version does not contain any statement for x^p + y^p = z^r or for signatures (p, p, r).
events.revisions: v4 22 Sep 2025 is the latest seen; the HTML header date of 24 Aug 2026 is unexplained.
events.delivers: Nonexistence for the factored equation with prime p > 3. Not the Beal equation, and not any stated (p, p, r) signature.
events.remains: Beal for every signature; the unfactored equation x^p + y^p = z^r.
events.doubts: Under review. Scope has changed across versions (p > 89, then q >= p >= 5, then p > 3). The survey's footnote 5 (dated April 2025, before this version) describes a Bartolome-Mihailescu claim for the signatures (p, p, r) with r > 3 sqrt(p log2 p) and says 'this paper has not been peer reviewed yet'; that wording is not in any version I read. The HTML date conflicts with the arXiv stamp.
events.direction: Toward nonexistence for the factored equation; not directly toward the Beal equation.

events.what_happened: Preda Mihailescu, 'The strong Fermat-Catalan Equation' (arXiv:2509.18275, v1 only, 22 Sep 2025). Abstract: 'We give a cyclotomic proof of the fact that the equation (x^p + y^p)/(x + y) = p^e z^q has no solutions in coprime integers x, y, z and p > 3; q, a pair of distinct odd primes.' The excerpt says the methods so far only handle a small set of primes p. This is the Fermat-Catalan form with a factor and a power of p, not Beal's equation.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Nonexistence for the factored Fermat-Catalan equation with p > 3 and q a distinct odd prime. A different equation, so it settles no Beal signature as stated.
events.remains: Beal's equation for all signatures.
events.doubts: Preprint; no referee or journal record found. Its own excerpt says earlier methods succeeded only for a small set of primes p.
events.direction: Toward nonexistence for a neighbouring equation only.

events.what_happened: Preprints.org manuscript 202109.0480 (author not confirmed). Search snippets show 'A Note on the Beal Conjecture' posted 19 Dec 2025, 'A Note on Fermat's Last Theorem' posted 27 Feb 2026 whose abstract still says the authors prove the Beal conjecture, and a latest version (v19) posted 16 Mar 2026. The platform labels it 'NOT PEER-REVIEWED'. The method is described in snippets as elementary (parametrisation of quadratic Diophantine equations, congruences). The page returned HTTP 403 on every attempt and was not opened. The 202109 prefix suggests an earlier origin in September 2021, which I could not confirm.
events.revisions: Multiple versions and titles (Dec 2025, Feb 2026, Mar 2026) per snippets; the 2021 origin is inferred from the ID.
events.delivers: As its abstract is said to read, a claim to the full conjecture. Not read.
events.remains: None, if the claim held.
events.doubts: Not opened. Claim known only from snippets. Platform label: not peer reviewed.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, as claimed.

events.what_happened: Ira Feinstein (Braid Council), 'Local Obstructions and Baker-Type Gap Bounds for the Beal Equation' (Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17166880, v1, published 20 Sep 2025). Abstract: a framework for primitive solutions with gcd(A, B, C) = 1, using congruence branches and Chinese Remainder Theorem moduli (worked example t = 24), and Baker/Matveev-type gap bounds giving a conditional cap M << (log H)^4 if an exponential upper bound on the gap is established. It states: 'The note does not resolve Beal's conjecture.'
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: No resolution. A computational framework and a conditional bound on the largest exponent under an unproven hypothesis. The local branch data cover only the branches the paper treats.
events.remains: The whole conjecture; the conditional bound needs an unproven gap estimate.
events.directly_checkable: The paper says it comes with verification scripts and tables with fixed random seeds (not inspected).
events.doubts: Explicitly not a resolution; its own conclusion is conditional. Zenodo's 'Journal' resource type is a label, not a peer-review statement.
events.direction: No direction on the conjecture's assertion; structural and conditional.

events.what_happened: Zhong-Peng Zhou, 'The inter-universal Teichmuller theory and new Diophantine results over rational numbers. II' (arXiv:2510.05448, math.NT, v1 6 Oct 2025, marked 'an older version of the paper, which will be updated soon'). Abstract: using IUT and a modified version for elliptic curves over Q, the generalised Fermat equation x^r + y^s = z^t has no non-trivial primitive solutions beyond the Catalan solution and nine non-Catalan solutions, for the signatures listed; corollary: 'to solve the Beal conjecture, we are left with 2446 signatures (r, s, t) up to permutation', and 244 remain for the generalised Fermat equation with all exponents >= 4. In the HTML v1 background list, the signatures (5, 5, q), primes q >= 11, are listed as 'proved elsewhere', citing Bartolome and Mihailescu, so (5, 5, 23) is outside the remaining set on Zhou's bookkeeping. The reference entry itself was not reached.
events.revisions: v1 6 Oct 2025 only; the arXiv listing read shows no v2 (the v2 abstract URL returned 404).
events.delivers: A reduction for Beal: the claim is that, after its results, 2446 signatures (up to permutation) remain. It settles no signature by itself; on Zhou's bookkeeping the (5, 5, q) signatures, q >= 11, are excluded by citation to Bartolome and Mihailescu.
events.remains: The Beal statement for the 2446 remaining signatures, including those that depend on the excluded families.
events.doubts: Relies on IUT, the theory whose key step Scholze and Stix (2018) said had an unfixable gap (Scientific American, 2020, opened); Kedlaya is quoted there as saying community opinion had not changed since 2018. The Beal reduction treats (5, 5, q), q >= 11, as settled by a citation to an unreviewed Bartolome-Mihailescu preprint whose versions read do not state that result. A search found press coverage (some of it aggregator) and an arXiv listing, but no mathematical engagement with the paper.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture only in the reduction sense; no counterexample; no full resolution.

events.what_happened: Devpost project 'Beal Conjecture solving for 3,5,7 using AI' (devpost.com/software/beal-conjecture-solving-for-3-5-7-using-ai), with an update dated 24 July 2026 (per search snippet). The snippet says the update reports eliminating certain branches for the exponent combination (3, 5, p), excluding some extension types, and running Magma verifications, with remaining obstacles: global non-split extension classes, including a surviving p = 7 case. Both the project page and the update returned HTTP 403 and were not opened; the description comes from a search snippet.
events.revisions: Project and update pages not read; the update date comes from a snippet.
events.delivers: Partial progress on signatures (3, 5, p): certain branches eliminated, per the snippet. Not a settled case. The survey (Ratcliffe and Grechuk, April 2025) says the smallest open triple is (3, 5, 7), so this bears on that open case.

events.what_happened: Shokir Davlatov, arXiv:1603.09665 (math.GM; comments 'in Russian'). The arXiv identifier has carried unrelated titles across versions (v3 Navier-Stokes, Dec 2020; v4 'fallibility of the Riemann hypothesis', Apr 2025; v10 'A Proof of the Riemann hypothesis', June 2025; v15 'Proof of the Collatz conjecture', Nov 2025). Beal content appears in v16 (12 Jan 2026, 'On the Beal Equation with Pairwise Coprime Bases'): 'In the first case, when the integers a,b,c are not pairwise coprime, the conclusion of Beal's conjecture follows immediately. In the second case, assuming that a,b,c are pairwise coprime, we provide a direct proof showing that the equation admits no solutions, without reducing the problem to Fermat's Last Theorem.' v17 (14 Jan 2026) withdrawn. v18 (16 Mar 2026, 'On the Beal Conjecture and the Nonexistence of Coprime Solutions for Exponents Greater than Two') claims 'the equation has no solutions in pairwise coprime integers when the exponents are greater than two', without the word 'proof'. v19 (25 Mar 2026) withdrawn; v20 (5 Apr 2026) and v21 (10 May 2026, withdrawn) are headed for the Riemann Hypothesis and a Salem-type integral equation.
events.revisions: Beal content: v16 12 Jan 2026 (claims both cases), v18 16 Mar 2026 (coprime case only); withdrawn: v17, v19, v21; v20 and v21 on other subjects. Versions v5-v9 and v11-v14 not individually opened.
events.delivers: If correct, the pairwise-coprime case, which is equivalent to the full conjecture (see problem_asks). So the claim covers every exponent triple, not a fragment. The non-coprime case reduces to the coprime case by the elementary observation that a prime dividing two bases divides the third; v16's claim there is correct as a reduction.
events.remains: None, if the claim held. The author's own v16 wording says the coprime case is settled by 'a direct proof'.
events.doubts: The same arXiv identifier carries unrelated papers across versions, and the author withdrew several versions. A withdrawal comment on the arXiv entry says that 'due to an error in the proof of the main result' the claimed proof of the Riemann Hypothesis should not be considered valid (the comment is on the RH version, not the Beal one). The Beal versions' proof text was not read. No referee or engagement found.

withdrawn.what: v17 (14 Jan 2026), v19 (25 Mar 2026) and v21 (10 May 2026) withdrawn by the author; the withdrawal comment on the RH version cites an error in the proof of the main result.

events.direction: Toward the conjecture, as claimed (full, via the coprime case).

events.what_happened: Anthropic, 'Formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem' (anthropic.com/research/formalizing-fermats-last-theorem, dated 4 Sep 2026; read via a fetch summary of the post, not verified verbatim). The post says Claude 'worked largely autonomously over 11 days to write the proof in the Lean programming language', producing about 13 million lines of Lean, 30,300 theorems proved and 29,500 used in the final proof, with 'dozens of Claude agents' coordinated through the Prove2Me platform. It says the proof follows a simplified version of Wiles's proof (Darmon, Diamond and Taylor) and uses 'just Lean's three standard axioms', with a comparator confirming the statement against Mathlib's. The post does not mention Beal's conjecture.
events.delivers: A formal verification of Fermat's Last Theorem: no positive solutions to x^n + y^n = z^n for n >= 3. That is the diagonal slice x = y = z of Beal's conjecture, already settled by Wiles (1995). It adds no new exponent triple and no new coprime solution form for Beal.
events.remains: Every exponent triple that is not all-equal, and the full Beal statement.

events.what_happened: Jeffery Huckstead, 'The Exponent Chamber Lift: Beal, Reciprocal Shells, and the First Hyperbolic Shadow' (Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20644786, published 11 Jun 2026, last modified 26 Jul 2026, file 'v1_3'). Abstract: 'It does not prove Beal's conjecture.' It builds a reciprocal-exponent atlas and notes that the first hyperbolic shell beyond the cubic corner, (3, 3, 4), 'is known to have no primitive positive solutions by Bruin's Chabauty and covering-method resolution'. It says a global proof would need 'a uniform obstruction for all hyperbolic exponent chambers'.
events.revisions: Listed as v2 on the record; file version 1.3 with a sharpened shell-envelope argument (26 Jul 2026).
events.delivers: None on the conjecture. A structural atlas of exponent chambers; restates the known (3, 3, 4) case.
events.remains: The whole conjecture.
events.doubts: The Zenodo 'Peer review' label is a resource-type classification, not a review statement. Not a claimed resolution.
events.direction: No direction on the conjecture's assertion.

events.what_happened: David Westerhoff (GitHub user dmwesterhoff; commit author shown as 'David Westerhoff and claude') published the repository 'beals' (MIT licence, described as 'Research toward Beal's conjecture') on 9 Oct 2026. README: 'New: x^5 + y^5 = z^23 has no non-trivial primitive solutions (unconditionally)', and the result 'settles Beal's conjecture for the signatures' (5, 5, 23), (5, 23, 5) and (23, 5, 5). docs/5-5-23.md states: 'No integers x, y, z with xyz != 0 and gcd(x, y, z) = 1 satisfy x^5 + y^5 = z^23', and 'settles the case (5, 5, 23) of Beal's conjecture'. Method: reduction to Stoll's curve 5y^2 = 4x^23 + 1 using Dahmen and Siksek's unconditional results; Stoll's criterion applied over L = Q(lambda), lambda^23 = 2; GRH removed by certifying that the class number of L is 1 (Zimmert's bound 273,676,831; explicit generators for 14,902,108 prime ideals; PARI/GP bnfcertify); and a PARI/GP reimplementation of Stoll's criterion, reproducing Stoll's Theorem 8.8 for 7 <= l <= 53. The README says 'Not yet confirmed: that it's new' and 'The authors haven't been asked'. The write-up says a novelty check (survey, Stoll's 2024 handout, 12 citing papers, web search) was done on 2026-10-09 and found no unconditional proof for p = 23. The repository also says its (5, 5, 11) result is 'Not a new case' because Stoll proved p <= 19 unconditionally.
events.revisions: 29 commits, all dated 9 Oct 2026 (00:59Z to 17:49Z). Initial commit 971c7d9 (README and gitignore) 00:59:57Z; repository created 00:59:58Z; last push 17:49:13Z. 23 commits carry the co-author trailer described under ai.
events.delivers: Claimed: the full Beal statement for the signature (5, 5, 23) and its two permutations, namely that every coprime solution of x^5 + y^5 = z^23 is trivial. Claimed to remove the GRH assumption that Stoll's 2015 result needed for p = 23. Nothing for any other signature, and no claim about GRH for other primes.
events.remains: Every other exponent signature (the repository's own next-case section points to other signatures); the full conjecture; and, unresolved, whether the Bartolome-Mihailescu line already covers (5, 5, q) for q >= 11 (see disputes).

machine_checked.system: PARI/GP 2.19.0 with the repository's own certification scripts, tests and CI (not a proof assistant)

events.directly_checkable: The README gives reproduction steps: build PARI/GP, run certify/setup.gp and units.gp, run certify/run_chunks.sh phase1 and generators, run check_results.py and pytest. The write-up estimates about 17 core-hours on an Apple M3 for the generator step and 2-3 hours on 8 cores for the rest. Not run here.
events.doubts: (1) Novelty is stated by the author as unconfirmed, and the authors had not asked experts. (2) The (5, 5, 23) case appears in unreviewed claims: survey footnote 5 and Zhou's background list cite Bartolome and Mihailescu for (p, p, r) or (5, 5, q), q >= 11; the versions I read do not contain that statement, so the novelty check's 'no unconditional proof for p = 23' may be incomplete. (3) The computation depends on a new PARI/GP reimplementation of Stoll's criterion (Stoll's code was Magma-only and unpublished, per the repository), so correctness rests on the repository's own tests and CI, not an outside reproduction. (4) The trust statements differ: the README's (5, 5, 11) entry says 'The one remaining trust assumption beyond PARI and Zimmert is Magma's 2-descent implementation', while docs/5-5-23.md says 'No step depends on GRH or on Magma' and cites Magma cross-checks (L({5},2) dimension 14). (5) It is two days old, and the repository has no referee or journal record. (6) It settles one signature out of infinitely many.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture's assertion for the signature (5, 5, 23): no coprime non-trivial solutions. No counterexample.
events.object: Not an exhibited object: a non-existence theorem for the equation x^5 + y^5 = z^23 with gcd(x, y, z) = 1. The argument shows that the rational points of Stoll's curve 5y^2 = 4x^23 + 1 are only the three obvious ones, via Stoll's criterion over Q(2^(1/23)), with the class number of that field certified as 1 by computation (Zimmert bound, prime-ideal generators checked in PARI/GP).

systems.name: Claude Opus 5.5
systems.what_it_did: Named as co-author in the trailers of 23 of the 29 commits. Commit subjects attribute the co-authored work to: the PARI/GP reimplementation of Stoll's Selmer-group criterion ('Reimplements Stoll's Selmer-group criterion in PARI/GP', 4b7455f); verification of factor-base generators for L23 (d879c34); the commit 'Unconditional (5,5,23) proof: generators, docs, CI' (2725d47), which adds docs/5-5-23.md, 133 files and CI; tests, lint, and CI; Magma cross-checks for L11. The README, the write-up docs/5-5-23.md and the commit body contain no statement about what the AI did or about AI in general. The mathematical reduction (Dahmen and Siksek; Stoll's criterion; the choice of field) is cited to published work rather than to the co-author. Whether the co-authored code is load-bearing for the claim is for the judging pass; the repository's own trust base names 'the correctness of the authors' reimplementation' as the key step beyond PARI and Zimmert.

disputes.summary: The 9 Oct 2026 (5, 5, 23) claim may not be the first to cover that signature. Survey footnote 5 (Ratcliffe and Grechuk, v2 14 Apr 2025) describes Bartolome and Mihailescu as claiming (1.2) for all signatures (p, p, r) with p >= 5 prime and r > 3 sqrt(p log2 p), which for p = 5 includes r = 23. Zhou's arXiv 2510.05448 (background list) treats (5, 5, q), q >= 11, as proved, citing Bartolome and Mihailescu. I could not find that statement in any Bartolome-Mihailescu version read (2108.08572 v1, v3, v4), which concern the factored equation (x^p + y^p)/(x + y) = p^e z^q or z^p with other bounds. Unresolved: the survey and Zhou may be citing a version not read, or misdescribing it.

Stoll (2015) states the (5, 5, p) result for p = 23 with GRH assumed (per the introduction read). The 2026 repository says it removes that assumption for p = 23 and that the result is 'Not yet confirmed: that it's new'. The claim is therefore a GRH-removal for one signature, not a first resolution of that signature, on the repository's own account.

The arXiv identifier 1603.09665 is shared by unrelated papers across versions (Navier-Stokes, Riemann Hypothesis, Collatz, Beal). Attributing the Beal versions to the same author rests on the listing's author field; the content of the entry changes with each version.

Zhou's arXiv 2510.05448 is described on Zhou's abstract as 'an older version' to be updated, and the arXiv listing read shows no v2. Its 2446 figure is therefore a claim of a single version whose exclusion of (5, 5, q) depends on a citation to an unreviewed Bartolome-Mihailescu preprint.

summary: I ran 39 web searches (listed below) and opened about 45 pages, including the Wikipedia article, arXiv abstracts and versions, Zenodo and Cambridge Open Engage records, the beals GitHub repository (README, write-up, commit list and one commit), the Ratcliffe-Grechuk survey (HTML v2, first 100,000 characters), Stoll's 2015 introduction (ar5iv), Norvig's search page, the Scientific American account of the IUT dispute, and Anthropic's FLT post (read through a fetch summary). Several sources returned HTTP 403 (Preprints.org, Figshare, the AMS prize page, Devpost) and are recorded as unopened. Nothing in the window has been accepted or refereed. Events fall into three groups. (i) Unrefereed full-proof claims: Vega (EasyChair, May and July 2024), Harris (Zenodo, July 2025), Hanners (Zenodo, 2025), Aabidi El Moussati (Cambridge Open Engage, May 2025), a Preprints.org manuscript (Dec 2025 onward, unopened), and Davlatov's arXiv entry, whose Beal content appears only in v16 (12 Jan 2026) and v18 (16 Mar 2026), with several withdrawals. The pairwise-coprime case Davlatov addresses is equivalent to the full conjecture, so these claims are all-or-nothing rather than partial. (ii) Partial or structural work: Zhou's IUT-based paper (arXiv 2510.05448, 6 Oct 2025, labelled an older version) says 2446 signatures (up to permutation) remain for Beal. It depends on IUT, whose key step Scholze and Stix (2018) said had an unfixable gap; I found no mathematical engagement with Zhou's paper. Zhou's background list also treats (5, 5, q), q >= 11, as proved, citing Bartolome and Mihailescu. Feinstein (Zenodo, Sept 2025) and Huckstead (Zenodo, June 2026) say explicitly that they do not resolve Beal. A Devpost project on the (3, 5, p) cases (update 24 Jul 2026, unopened) is titled 'using AI' but names no system in the snippet. (iii) The one claim that settles a single signature: the GitHub repository beals, created 9 Oct 2026, says x^5 + y^5 = z^23 has no coprime non-trivial solutions, unconditionally, using a PARI/GP reimplementation of Stoll's criterion and a certified class number of Q(2^(1/23)). Stoll's 2015 introduction gives the same (5, 5, 23) result conditional on GRH, so the repository claims a GRH removal for one signature. Its author writes that novelty is not confirmed. Twenty-three of its 29 commits carry the trailer 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5', while the README and write-up say nothing about AI, so what the model did is inferable only from commit subjects. On the AI search generally: I found no AI-attributed claim on Beal beyond that trailer and the unopened Devpost title. The Anthropic FLT formalisation (4 Sep 2026, Claude, read via a fetch summary) covers the diagonal x = y = z, which Wiles settled in 1995, so it adds nothing to Beal. The OpenAI 722-manuscript release (6 Oct 2026) shows no Beal entry in its README or in the 55 of about 372 catalogue headings I could read, so this is incomplete. Close calls: (a) whether the Bartolome-Mihailescu citations make (5, 5, 23) already claimed, which decides whether the repository adds a new signature; (b) whether a commit trailer is 'the authors' own account' of a load-bearing AI contribution, which the write-up does not confirm; (c) whether an outcome counts as partial when the reduction (Zhou) relies on an unreviewed citation.
competing_reading: Read the beals repository as a real, if single-signature, advance: the certification is mechanical and its trust base is stated, CI reruns the computation, and Stoll's 2015 result was conditional on GRH for this exponent, so the repository removes a condition. On that reading one signature (5, 5, 23) is settled since 26 Jan 2024, with AI co-authorship disclosed in commit trailers, and a judging pass would count it as a partial result. The contrary reading treats it as a two-day-old, unconfirmed, AI co-authored computation of a single signature whose novelty may be covered by an existing unreviewed Bartolome-Mihailescu claim, so it adds no settled case. For the full-proof claims, the opposite error is also possible: because the coprime form is equivalent to the full conjecture, a valid version of any of them would settle the problem outright, and the record's failure to find a checker is not evidence that the arguments are wrong.
what_would_settle_it: (1) An independent rerun of the beals computation, the generator and Phase 1 outputs and the Stoll-criterion reimplementation, by a number theorist or by Stoll or Siksek. (2) The authors' answer on novelty against Stoll (2015) Theorem 8.8, and a check of whether any Bartolome-Mihailescu version states a result for x^5 + y^5 = z^q with q >= 11: the survey's reference [3] and Zhou's bibliography entry, neither of which I reached. (3) A referee report or journal record for the (5, 5, 23) result, and for Zhou's 2510.05448. (4) Zhou's own treatment of (5, 5, 23) in the full text (beyond the first 100,000 characters read). (5) For the AI question: the repository owner's account of what Claude produced, which code, which argument, and which steps the mathematics depends on; the commit trailer alone does not say. (6) For the Davlatov and other full-proof claims: a proof text checked by a qualified reader. The Devpost project's full update would settle what the 'using AI' label means for the (3, 5, p) case.

incomplete: (1) Not opened because of HTTP 403: Preprints.org 202109.0480 and 202501.1436, Figshare 6217232, Devpost (project and update), the AMS Beal Prize page. Their events are recorded from snippets and marked accordingly; the Devpost update is the only item that bears directly on the AI question for an open signature, and its AI attribution is unverified. (2) The Ratcliffe-Grechuk reference list was not reached, so footnote 5's reference [3] (the Bartolome-Mihailescu citation) is unresolved. Zhou's bibliography entry was not reached either. The (p, p, r) statement attributed to Bartolome and Mihailescu does not appear in any version I read, and v2 (14 Oct 2021) was not read. (3) Stoll 2015 Theorem 8.8 (the exact GRH statement for p = 23) was not reached; the ar5iv fetch was truncated before Section 8. (4) Zhou II's full text was read only to 100,000 characters, so its treatment of (5, 5, 23) and of the IUT objection is incomplete. (5) The Davlatov versions v5 to v9 and v11 to v14 were not opened; the claim that the Beal content first appears in v16 rests on the versions read. (6) Pre-2024 partial results are recorded as grouped events drawn from the Wikipedia article's list; the individual papers (Bruin 2003, Poonen-Schaefer-Stoll 2005, Bennett et al. 2014, Dahmen-Siksek 2013, and others) were not opened, and the list is not exhaustive. Dahmen-Siksek's GRH cases are from a search snippet. (7) OpenAI's 722 manuscripts: only 55 catalogue headings were read, and the Fermat-type result that the press mentions was not located, so a Beal-relevant entry cannot be excluded. (8) The Hanners and Harris records were read from their Zenodo pages; their proofs were not read. (9) Anthropic's FLT post was read through a fetch summary; quotations are not verified verbatim. (10) The AMS award rules and the 2013 committee text are from snippets only. (11) I did not run the beals reproduction commands, and I did not check the author's claimed compute figures. (12) No journal or referee record was searched for each claim beyond a general search; a targeted check of Mathematical Reviews or zbMATH for each named author was not made.
